anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Critical metadata about row counts, data distribution, and correlations is stale, missing, or inaccurate, causing systematic cardinality misestimation by the optimizer.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: Despite acceptable or refreshed statistics, the optimizer’s plan–choice logic (cost model, parameter sniffing, cache reuse, hinting, etc.) selects execution plans that are substantially sub-optimal for the current runtime context.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly: Downstream replicas or subscribers cannot receive, write, or apply redo at the rate the primary generates it, producing widening log-position gaps, replay lag, and retention of excessive log files on the primary.

When these three root causes manifest simultaneously, a workload may show oscillating or chronically poor query performance on the primary, skyrocketing redo generation, and rapidly growing replication lag. Stale or incomplete statistics combine with an already fragile plan-selection process to create highly variable, often bloated execution plans—e.g., hash joins degraded to nested loops or full-table scans materializing large intermediate results. The resultant surge in I/O, CPU, and log volume prolongs transaction durations and inflates redo streams. Replicas struggle to keep pace, leading to seconds-to-hours of apply lag, swollen relay/WAL files, stale read-only query results, and reduced failover readiness. Because replicas replay long-running, poorly planned transactions serially, their apply workers may become backlogged or blocked by lock contention, further compounding lag.

Causally, inaccurate statistics seed cardinality errors that steer the optimizer toward fragile plans; even if statistics are corrected, plan-selection anomalies (e.g., parameter sniffing or cost-model quirks) may continue to favor inefficient strategies. These inefficient plans inflate resource consumption and transaction sizes, multiplying redo output. The heavier the write volume and transaction duration, the more pressure is placed on the replication pipeline. Conversely, replication lag prevents timely feedback such as replicated statistics refreshes or plan–stability hint deployments on replicas, allowing bad plans to persist there as well. The intertwined feedback loop—bad stats ⇒ bad plans ⇒ high redo ⇒ replication backlog ⇒ delayed metadata convergence—drives a self-reinforcing degradation that affects both primary performance and replica consistency.

entry.official_definition: The execution timeout for SELECT statements, in milliseconds.
entry.trigger_condition: A SELECT statement exceeds the configured max_execution_time limit.
entry.workload_impact: The SELECT statement is interrupted by the execution time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
